title: Unauthenticated debug route exposes effective tool configuration for arbitrary user_id
reasoning: The network-facing GET route accepts caller-controlled tool_name and user_id/model/provider query parameters, resolves an effective debug config, and returns the config plus canonical/provider tool capability schemas. The handler has no visible authentication, authorization, or debug-mode guard dependency. If this router is reachable outside a trusted local context, a caller can enumerate tool capability/config details for arbitrary user IDs, which is a permission and information-disclosure gap.
recommendation: Require an authenticated or explicitly local/debug-only dependency for this route, and authorize the requested user_id against the caller before resolving or returning the effective config. If this endpoint is intended to be local-only, enforce that invariant at the route or router dependency level rather than relying on deployment assumptions.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for this feature, and the shown handler has no assertion-enforced auth or debug gating behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test that unauthenticated requests to /api/sdk/tool-capabilities/{tool_name} are rejected, and that an authenticated caller cannot request another user's effective config unless explicitly authorized.
minimumFixScope: Add route/router-level auth or debug-local guard and cover sdk_debug_tool_capabilities with focused API tests.
